h1: The 8 Best Bissell Carpet Cleaners of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bissell Carpet Cleaners: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 Bissell carpet cleaners compared on tank size, pet stain tools and portability, from ProHeat 2X to Little Green.
summary: The ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus is the best overall for pet households with real carpet to clean, thanks to its CleanShot pretreater. The TurboClean Pet XL is the better value for most families, with a 10 inch path and a 1 gallon tank. The Big Green suits heavy use, the TurboClean line fits apartments, and the two Little Green models handle stairs, upholstery and cars.
intro: Bissell sells carpet cleaners in three shapes that have almost nothing in common: full-size uprights, the Big Green commercial-style machine, and the pint-size Little Green portables. The classic buyer error is choosing by brand loyalty instead of shape. A portable will take a week to do one living room, and a heavy upright rots in a closet if you only own a stair runner and a couch.

Our editors reviewed eight Bissell models from their listings and ranked them on tank size, stain tools, pet features and storage footprint. Where a listing leaves out a spec, such as weight or tank capacity, we say so rather than guess, and the missing detail counts against the pick.

products.name: BISSELL ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: A pet-focused whole-home cleaner with a pretreater for set-in stains and odors.
products.description:
The ProHeat is the pet-household machine of the group. Its CleanShot pretreater goes onto stains before the wash cycle, so cleaner has time to work on set-in marks and odors that a single pass would skip. StainProtect is meant to keep treated spots from wicking back up, and the listing puts a standard cycle at about 30 minutes of drying.

It outranks the TurboClean line by being the more complete system, and it costs more, in the $200 to $500 bucket. Against the Big Green it is easier to live with, though its tank is smaller than that machine's 1.75 gallons.

Buy it for a house with pets and plenty of carpet. Skip it if you own one rug; you would be paying for pretreater hardware you rarely use.
pros: StainProtect to help spots stay gone
products.idealFor: Pet owners cleaning whole rooms of carpet.
products.skipIf: You only have a few small rugs.

products.name: BISSELL TurboClean Pet XL Upright Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: A 10-inch clean path and a 1-gallon tank. The sweet spot for a typical home.
products.description:
The Pet XL is the middle ground that suits most family homes. A 10 inch clean path covers more carpet per pass than the compact models, and a 1 gallon tank cuts refill trips well below what any portable manages. Above-floor attachments reach baseboards and stairs, so one machine covers more than the floor.

It ranks second because it does much of the ProHeat's job at a lower price, in the $100 to $200 bucket, but lists no dedicated pretreater. That absence shows on old, set-in stains. It beats the plain TurboClean with the wider path and bigger tank.

Choose it for mid-size carpeted rooms and everyday spills. Do not expect it to match the ProHeat on deep pet stains.
cons: Bigger than the portables to store
products.skipIf: You need to treat old set-in stains aggressively.

products.name: BISSELL Big Green Professional Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: The largest tank here at 1.75 gallons, with forward and backward passes.
products.description:
Big Green is the commercial-style heavyweight. Its tank holds 1.75 gallons, the largest of the eight, which means fewer stops mid-room. It cleans on both the forward and backward pass, covering more ground per stroke and, per the listing, drying faster. A stain tool handles corners.

It ranks third because it is the most expensive here and the hardest to store, and its pet tech is less targeted than the ProHeat's pretreater. The Pet XL gives up capacity but weighs less on the budget and the floor space.

Buy it if you clean large areas often, or run a rental property. For a one-bedroom apartment it is far too much machine, and stairs will be a chore with something this large.
products.skipIf: You have limited storage or small rooms.

products.name: BISSELL TurboClean Upright Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: A compact, lightweight upright with a 4-row DeepReach brush for small homes.
products.description:
The plain TurboClean is the small-space upright. A four row DeepReach brush works fibers loose, and the compact, lightweight body is sized for apartments and area rugs. Easy storage matters more than people admit; a machine that fits a closet gets used.

It sits below the Pet XL because its reach is smaller and it lists no pet formula or extra pet tools. It does cost less, and on a full rug it still outcleans any portable here.

It fits dorms, apartments and starter homes with limited carpet. If animals live with you, step up to the Pet XL or the TurboClean PET. The listing does not state tank capacity, so check before you rely on it for a whole bedroom.
products.idealFor: Apartment dwellers and area rug owners.
products.skipIf: You have lots of carpet or pets.

products.name: BISSELL TurboClean PET
products.verdict: A compact upright with a 7-foot hose, a 4-inch tool and a spraying attachment.
products.description:
The TurboClean PET is the attachment specialist. It ships with a 7 foot hose, a 4 inch self-cleanout tool that purges itself with one touch, and a spraying attachment. Those tools matter on stairs and furniture, where a floor head cannot reach.

It ranks below the Pet XL because the XL lists the wider path and a 1 gallon tank, while this model does not give a tank size. Against the plain TurboClean, you gain the pet-focused accessories at a similar step in price.

Buy it if pets mean frequent stair and couch messes and your space is tight. The caveat is coverage: a compact body with a smaller reach means more passes across a large living room.
pros: Self-cleanout tool clears in one touch
cons: Smaller reach than the Pet XL
products.idealFor: Pet owners who need stair and upholstery tools.
products.skipIf: You want the widest clean path.

products.name: BISSELL Revolution HydroSteam Pet Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: HydroSteam technology aimed at stuck-on and sticky messes.
products.description:
HydroSteam is the pitch here: technology aimed at stuck-on, sticky messes such as dried juice, with a pet formula behind it. Purchases also support the brand's pet rescue foundation, which some buyers will weigh.

It ranks sixth because the listing leaves out the tank size and tool list, which makes it hard to judge against the TurboClean models it costs more than. It also sits in the $200 to $500 bucket, the same tier as the ProHeat, which is the more fully specified pet machine.

Pick it only if sticky spills are your main problem and you can confirm the tank size and tools with the seller. Otherwise the Pet XL gives you clearer specs for less money.
products.idealFor: Homes with sticky spills and pets.
products.skipIf: You want a clearly specified tank and tool list.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Multi-Purpose Portable Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: A portable spot cleaner for stairs, upholstery and car interiors.
products.description:
The Multi-Purpose Little Green is a portable spot cleaner for stairs, upholstery and car interiors. Its clean-water tank is large for a portable, which means fewer refills when you work through a set of stairs or a car's seats, and it stores in a cupboard.

It ranks seventh because no portable can clean a room efficiently. A room-sized job means many passes and many refills. Against the Mini it holds more water, so it covers more spot jobs per fill.

Buy it for pet accidents, couch cushions and the car. It is the right second machine for a household that already has an upright. As a single cleaner for a carpeted house it will frustrate you, and the listing gives no wattage or suction figure to reassure you.
pros: Large clean-water tank for a portable
products.idealFor: Spot cleaning stairs, couches and car seats.
products.skipIf: You need to clean full rooms.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: The cheapest Bissell here, with a 4-inch tough stain tool and self-cleaning hose.
products.description:
The Mini is the cheapest Bissell here, in the $50 to $100 bucket. It includes a 4 inch tough stain tool and a self-cleaning HydroRinse hose tool, which rinses itself so cleaner residue does not sit in the line. The body is small and light enough for a dorm shelf.

It ranks last because it has the smallest capacity of the eight. It does the same spot work as the Multi-Purpose, but with less tank, so a few spots exhaust a fill.

It makes a sensible first cleaner for a dorm or small apartment with occasional spills. Do not expect it to handle a large stain or a whole room. If you can spend a bit more, the Multi-Purpose offers a larger tank.
products.idealFor: Dorms and apartments with occasional spills.
products.skipIf: You need to clean whole rooms.

methodology.title: Fit to the job
methodology.description: We ranked each machine against the cleaning job it is built for, since a spot cleaner and an upright are not comparable.

methodology.title: Tank and path
methodology.description: Tank size and clean path width were compared because they decide how often you refill and how long a room takes.

methodology.title: Pet tools
methodology.description: Pretreaters, formulas and hose tools counted for homes with pets.

methodology.title: Storage footprint
methodology.description: Bulk and weight affect whether you actually take the machine out, so size was weighed.

methodology.title: Value in the field
methodology.description: Features were judged against price tier relative to the other seven Bissell models.

whatMatters.detail: Machine shape should follow carpet area. A portable spot cleaner suits stairs, a car and a couch, a compact upright suits an apartment, and a large upright suits a whole house. Estimate how many square feet you actually clean, then pick the shape. The wrong shape wastes either time or space. Compare product type in the title.

whatMatters.factor: Check the tank, not only the motor
whatMatters.detail: Tank size sets how many refills each room needs, and refills break your rhythm. A 1 gallon tank means fewer trips than a portable, and the Big Green's 1.75 gallons goes further still. Many listings, such as the TurboClean PET and HydroSteam, omit it. Find capacity in the bullets, and ask the seller if it is missing.

A pretreater applies cleaner to a stain before the wash so it can dwell, and a pet formula is tuned for urine and protein stains. Pet messes set deep, so skipping the dwell step leaves odors behind. Look for the words pretreater, CleanShot or pet formula on the listing, and expect to use a stain tool on old spots.

Wet carpet attracts new dirt and smells if it stays damp for hours. Dry time depends on how much water the machine leaves behind and on ventilation. The ProHeat listing cites roughly 30 minutes on a standard cycle. Look for a stated figure, and open windows or run a fan to speed it along.

A big upright is heavy and takes closet space, so many owners stop using it. Storage footprint is therefore a real buying factor, not an afterthought. Measure the space you plan to use, then compare it with the machine's listed size or category. A compact upright or portable you use often beats a stronger machine in the basement.

faq.q: Which Bissell carpet cleaner is best for pets?
faq.a: The ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus, thanks to its CleanShot pretreater and StainProtect. The TurboClean PET is the cheaper pet option, with a 7 foot hose and a spray attachment, but it lacks the pretreater for older stains.

faq.q: Is a Little Green enough for a whole room?
faq.a: No. Both Little Green models are spot cleaners for stairs, upholstery and cars. A whole room means many passes and refills, so use a TurboClean or ProHeat upright for floors and keep the Little Green for accidents.

faq.q: How long do carpets take to dry?
faq.a: The ProHeat listing says about 30 minutes on a standard cycle. Thick carpet, a damp room or poor airflow lengthens that. The Big Green's forward and backward passes are said to dry faster, though no figure is given.

faq.q: Is the Big Green worth it for home use?
faq.a: Only if you clean large areas often or manage rentals. Its 1.75 gallon tank is the biggest here, but it is bulky to store. For a normal house the Pet XL, with a 1 gallon tank, is easier.

faq.q: Is the TurboClean Pet XL better than the standard TurboClean?
faq.a: For most homes, yes. The Pet XL adds a 10 inch clean path, a 1 gallon tank and above-floor tools. The plain TurboClean suits small apartments and area rugs, where its compact body is the advantage.

faq.q: Can I use these on upholstery and stairs?
faq.a: Yes. The TurboClean PET ships with a 7 foot hose and stair tools, and the Pet XL has above-floor attachments. The Little Green models are built for stairs, couches and car seats, though their small tanks limit each session.

finalTake: Buy the ProHeat if pets and set-in stains are the problem, and the TurboClean Pet XL if you want most of that performance for less. Move to the Big Green only when you clean carpet constantly. For apartments pick the plain TurboClean, and add a Little Green only as a second tool for spills, never as your main cleaner.
